headline: Baby talk, a lonely lunch and a flying bowl
teaser: When do babies say their first word? Why does Leo always eat alone? What happens when Nadia starts the pottery wheel too fast?

articles.title: How Do Babies Learn to Talk?
articles.dek: Nobody gives babies lessons, but they learn a language in two years. How?

sources.name: Mayo Clinic: Language development – speech milestones for babies
PubMed: Effects of experience on fetal voice recognition (2003)

paras: How do babies learn to talk? They can't read books, and nobody gives them lessons. But by the age of two, most children can say a lot of words. So what happens in those first two years? Let's find out.

When does a baby start learning? The answer is surprising: before it is born! In the last months before birth, a baby can hear sounds from outside. Scientists have found that babies know their mother's voice. In one study, a baby's heart beat faster when it heard its mother. It beat more slowly when a stranger spoke.

What do babies do in their first months? They listen all the time. They also cry, smile and make happy noises. At about six months, most babies start to babble. They say sounds like 'ba-ba-ba' and 'da-da-da'. These sounds have no meaning yet. But this is how babies practise. They learn to use their mouths and tongues.

Which words come first? Many babies say their first real word at about twelve months. Often it is a short, easy word like 'mama', 'dada' or 'uh-oh'. Babies usually understand more words than they can say. A baby hears 'Where's your ball?' and looks at the ball. But the baby can't say 'ball' yet.

How many words do children know at eighteen months? Many children can say about fifty words. After that, they learn new words very fast. At about two years old, they start to put two words together. They say things like 'more milk' or 'Daddy gone'.

How can families help? Talk to your baby a lot. Read picture books together, sing songs and answer the baby's sounds. Every child is different. Some babies talk early, and some talk later. And here is a question for you: what was your first word? Why not ask your parents tonight?

articles.title: Leo Eats Alone
articles.dek: Leo always eats lunch by himself. Then a new girl sits down next to him.
paras: Leo was fourteen, and he was very shy. Every day at lunch, he sat by himself in the corner of the canteen. He ate his sandwich quickly and read a book. The other students didn't really know him, and he didn't talk to them.

One Monday, a new girl came into the canteen with her tray. Her name was Ana, and she was from Brazil. She looked around, but all the tables were full. Then she saw Leo. 'Can I sit with you?' she asked him. Leo was surprised, but he said yes.

Ana talked a lot. She told him about her old school in Brazil and her two cats. 'I don't know anyone here,' she said. 'I feel a bit lonely.' Leo understood her. He often felt the same. So he told her about his favourite thing: the school chess club.

'Chess? I love chess!' said Ana. 'My grandfather taught me.' Leo wanted to invite her to the club. But he couldn't say the words. He was angry with himself. After lunch, Ana went to her class, and Leo walked home by himself again.
That evening, Leo looked at himself in the mirror. 'Come on,' he said to himself. 'Just ask her. It's easy.' He said the question three times. The fourth time, it sounded quite good.

The next day, Leo found Ana in the canteen. This time he spoke first. 'Would you like to come to chess club with me on Wednesday?' he asked. Ana smiled. 'Yes, please! Can I bring my friend Sam? He wants to learn too.'

On Wednesday, Ana and Sam came to the club. Ana won two games. Sam didn't know the rules, so Leo taught him. They laughed a lot that afternoon, and they all enjoyed themselves. Now Leo never eats lunch by himself. He sits with them every day.

articles.title: My First Pottery Class
articles.dek: Nadia tries to make a bowl – and her clay flies across the room!
paras: Hi everyone! It's Nadia again. Last Saturday I tried a new hobby: pottery. My aunt gave me a class for my birthday. I was excited, but I was nervous too. I'm not very good at art!

The class was in a small studio near the river. There were six students and a teacher called Mr Okafor. He spoke quietly and smiled a lot. First, he showed us the clay. It was cold, wet and very heavy. My hands got dirty very quickly!

Then we sat at the pottery wheels. The wheel turns round and round, and you make a bowl on it with your hands. Mr Okafor showed us first. He worked slowly and carefully, and a beautiful bowl grew in his hands. It looked so easy!

It wasn't easy for me. I started the wheel too fast, and my clay flew off! It landed on the floor with a big noise. Everybody laughed, and I laughed loudly too. Mr Okafor helped me patiently. 'Don't hurry,' he said. 'Move your hands gently.'

My second try went much better. I pressed the clay softly and kept my hands still. Slowly, a little bowl appeared. It wasn't perfect. One side was higher than the other. But it was mine, and I was really proud of it.

Next week, we're going to paint our bowls. Then Mr Okafor is going to put them in a very hot oven. I want to give my bowl to my aunt. She can put her keys in it or use it for sweets. Have you ever tried pottery? Tell me in the comments!

grammar.rule: Adverbs of manner tell us how someone does something. Most are adjective + -ly: quiet → quietly, careful → carefully. If the adjective ends in -y, change it to -ily (easy → easily); -le becomes -ly (gentle → gently). Some are different: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard.

He worked slowly and carefully, and a beautiful bowl grew in his hands.
I pressed the clay softly and kept my hands still.

Mr Okafor worked slowly and carefully and made a beautiful bowl.
Nadia started the wheel too fast, and her clay flew off.
kps.q: What went wrong on the first try?

kps.fact: On her second try, Nadia made a little bowl and felt proud.
kps.q: How did Nadia feel about her bowl?

kps.fact: Next week the students are going to paint their bowls.
kps.q: What will they do next week?

mindmap.question: How did Nadia make her first bowl?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the blog post.
summary.model: Nadia went to her first pottery class, but her clay flew off the wheel. She tried again slowly, so she made a little bowl.

options.t: Nadia went to her first pottery class last Saturday.
options.why: This is what the whole post is about.
options.evidence: Last Saturday I tried a new hobby: pottery.

options.t: Her first try went wrong because the wheel was too fast.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraph 4.
options.evidence: I started the wheel too fast, and my clay flew off!

options.t: On her second try, she made a little bowl and felt proud.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraph 5.
options.evidence: But it was mine, and I was really proud of it.

options.t: There were six students in the class.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: There were six students and a teacher called Mr Okafor.

options.t: Nadia wants to sell her bowl at the market.

speak.p: Tell me about a new hobby you want to try. Why do you want to try it?
speak.hint: I want to try … because … / I think it is …

write.p: You went to a new class (art, music or sport) last weekend. Write an email to your friend. Write 25 words or more.
steps: Say what class you went to.
Say how the teacher did things (slowly, patiently…).
Say if you want to go again and why.
